rule.description: A concrete participant of an abc.ABC frontend contract locally implements a contract-declared capability that no live production dispatch reaches on that class: liveness starts at driver entry points outside the contract classes and propagates only through members already known live, so self-references inside never-dispatched members do not count as usage.

checks.description: For every concrete frontend class, report each fat-contract member it implements for which no production call path dispatches on that class.
checks.detected_relation: abstract contract member (declared by frontends.FuzzFrontend) -> local implementation on a concrete bundled frontend -> no live dispatch on that participant
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The uniform frontend interface exceeds the dependency boundary of most bundled generator families: DOM bookkeeping, GPU shader introspection and registry hooks are required of implementors whose own pipelines never exercise them, and the forced bodies are plausible-looking per-family implementations that no runtime path reaches - the interface-segregation violation.

excluded.description: Abstract, non-instantiable contract classes (FuzzFrontend, DocumentFuzzFrontend, ShaderFuzzFrontend) are not report owners: they inherit abstract requirements rather than being forced to implement unused capabilities.

Members without a local implementation on a participant (e.g. write_samples and load_template_file inherited from the intermediate bases) are outside the rule: only locally implemented forced bodies are credited.

Live pipeline members (load_grammars, generate_new_sample, generate_function_body; the DOM family's element bookkeeping trio; WebGPU's collect_shader_entrypoints/collect_shader_bindings) are exercised by real dispatch and therefore never reported.

Dunder and underscore-prefixed members, test files (never among the analysis units), and usages whose receiver class cannot be attributed are outside the rule (the latter suppress the member conservatively).
